svg.title: A search, pass by pass
svg.desc: A query groups a clip's rows by hash. Each hash is looked up in every segment's directory; the totals pass counts votes per reference in dense counters, capped by the fanout; references whose totals reach the vote floor survive; the histogram pass turns each survivor's votes into offsets and bins them; each survivor's best bin and the noise around it become a candidate.
svg.text: Every vote the caps allow is counted and nothing is sampled. Chance matches stop at step 3, so only survivors pay for a histogram.
(hash, time) rows by hash and keeps each hash's first 64 times. The
cap bounds what one hash that is common in the clip can cost.
Each query hash is looked up in every segment's directory: one read.
A slot depends only on the hash, so the reads are independent; slots
are loaded 32 ahead and the cache misses overlap. Each hit is a run:
a hash split across segments is several runs
For every run, each posting adds its hash's kept query times to its
reference's counter: totals[reference] += times. At most the
fanout (64) postings of one (hash, reference) vote, the first by
time; a run whose mult is at or under the fanout skips that test. The
lines of the next 16 runs are loaded ahead, and with simd eight
totals: one u32 per reference id
hashes with the clip; the rest are chance
One scan of the counters: a live reference whose total reaches
min_total_votes survives (vote_floor scales it with the query:
84 for 4,200 rows). Counters reset as they are read. Before any
histogram work: TotalsOverflow, TooManyVotes past max_votes.
The runs are walked again for survivors only (a bitmap test where a run
has many, a binary search where it has few). Each vote becomes
(Δ = reference time − query time, query time); votes are grouped
by survivor, sorted by Δ and merged into bins: votes, first and last time.
The bin with most votes (ties to the smaller Δ) becomes a Candidate;
bins outside ±offset_tolerance (2) of it give the noise: count, mean,
deviation, max. search_with hands your closure the bins instead.
Scratch, one per thread, holds the counters (4 bytes and a bit per id), runs, groups, votes (16 bytes each) and bins, reused across searches.
